events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southeast Louisiana, including the following
parishes, Central Jefferson, Central Plaquemines, Central St.
Charles, Central Tangipahoa, Coastal Jefferson, Eastern Orleans,
Lower Plaquemines, Lower St. Bernard, Lower St. Charles, Lower
Tangipahoa, Northern St. Tammany, Northern Tangipahoa, Southeast
St. Tammany, Southwestern St. Tammany, St. John The Baptist, Upper
Jefferson, Upper Plaquemines, Upper St. Bernard, Upper St. Charles,
Washington and Western Orleans and southern Mississippi, including
the following counties, Pearl River, Pike and Walthall.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms producing locally
heavy rainfall are expected through this evening. Additional
rainfall amounts of 3 to 5 inches with locally higher amounts are
possible in the watch area through midnight Sunday evening.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.region: Transylvania, NC; Oconee, SC; Pickens, SC
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Southwestern Transylvania County in western North
Carolina...
Northeastern Oconee County in upstate South Carolina...
Northwestern Pickens County in upstate South Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 315 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 144 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain. Minor flooding
is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the advisory area.
Between 3.5 and 5.5 inches of rain have fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Rosman, Jocassee Gorges, Lake Jocassee, Gorges State Park, Keowee
Toxaway State Park, Devils Fork State Park, Table Rock State
Park, Lake Keowee, Rocky Bottom and Sunset.
- Nuisance to minor flooding is possible along Mill Creek Road west
of Sunset, Rocky Bottom Road and F Van Clayton Memorial Highway
in Rocky Bottom in northwestern Pickens County, Abby Falls Drive,
Oscar Chappell Road, Frozen Creek Road, Old CC Road, and Devils
Hole Road in southern Transylvania County, and Sumter National
Forest in northeastern Oconee County.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

burning is not recommended.
